key_insight: LLMPopSim shows that individually simulated AI agents can be aggregated into population-level health patterns that partly match real-world screening behavior across places and time.
clinical_relevance: This could help researchers test public health interventions and estimate community-level behavior without relying only on costly or delayed survey data.
method: Built AI agent populations using U.S. Census and CDC data
Tested transfer to 2022 Hawaii and New York State for colorectal cancer screening and mammography
evidence_signal: Across four state-outcome tests, mean absolute error was 3.5 to 15.0 percentage points and ZCTA-level correlations ranged from 0.26 to 0.69.
watch_item: The model showed notable bias and weaker performance in lower-prevalence communities, so calibration and subgroup fidelity remain important concerns.
paper_title: Evaluating agentic simulation for local public health estimation
